text:
marina: quick heads-up — dropped a new mock for the alerting preview: ordering of 'urgency' pills + snooze gap UI. link: https://figma.com/file/alert-preview-urgency
devon: looks good, thanks. are the urgency pills meant to reflect routing priority or just visual weight?
alex: they should map to routing tiers. iirc infra wants highest priority first so routing and preview match.
marina: yep routing tiers — high / medium / low. the tricky bit is the snooze gap indicator between two alerts (we show a tiny waveform). thinking about clarity and a11y.
priya: waveform is cute but low-contrast for screen readers. can we add a textual label like "snooze gap: 2h" visible in DOM?
daniela: +1 to textual label. also for compact mode what happens when pills overflow? current mock collapses to "+2" which is ambiguous. maybe show a summary tooltip with counts by urgency.
marina: good call. proposed change: collapsed state shows "+N (H/M/L)" e.g., "+2 (1/1/0)" — short but more informative. thoughts?
devon: that could be noisy. maybe make it optional via user preference? default to simple "+2" and reveal counts on hover / focus.
alex: hover is fine but keyboard users need focusable element. ensure the collapsed pill is a button with aria-expanded? even if it doesn't expand, it should have aria-describedby linking to the tooltip content.
a11y-bot: automated check: tooltip must be accessible on focus and activated with keyboard; ensure role="tooltip" paired with aria-describedby on target. color contrast for pills should be minimum 3:1 for decorative small text.
priya: also callout: the urgency colors are red/orange/blue in the mock — red and orange meet contrast? probably not for body text. use 16px bold or increase contrast.
daniela: copy nit on the snooze control — label currently "Snooze gap" confused me. maybe "Quiet window" or "Suppression gap"? internal consistency with our other UIs is important.
marina: i'd prefer "Quiet window" to match other flows. i'll update mocks.
devon: one more runtime question: when preview shows routed channels, do we surface fallback channel inline? product asked for visibility into fallbacks for on-call.
alex: show fallback as a dimmed pill with dotted border and tooltip explaining "fallback when primary unavailable". same keyboard/accessibility rules apply.
marina: summary of actions: 1) change label to "Quiet window" 2) add textual snooze gap in DOM 3) collapse pill to "+N (H/M/L)" on hover, default "+N" 4) ensure collapsed pill is keyboard focusable with aria-describedby 5) adjust color contrast for urgency colors 6) add fallback pill style and tooltip. i'll post updated frames by EOD.
priya: thanks! small follow-up — can we include a screenreader-only announcement when preview toggles between compact/expanded so users know channel ordering changed?
a11y-bot: recommended: use live region with aria-live="polite" and briefly announce "Preview updated: 3 channels, primary: PagerDuty". keep messages short.
marina: noted, will add aria-live region text. anyone want to pair on the tooltip a11y test?
daniela: happy to pair tomorrow morning.
devon: i'll update the design doc with the routing implications for Dedicated customers (they care about explicit fallback visibility).
marina: awesome — thanks everyone. tagging @design-critique for FYI :thumbsup:
marina: (attached: figma frames + small screen recording of compact->expanded interaction)
